name: vscode-portal
description: Use your Mac from your iPhone: run Claude Code, edit files live, review diffs, commit and push, and see and control the whole screen.

commands.title: VSCode Portal: Turn On Screen Sharing

vscodePortal.enabled.description: Start the phone server when VS Code opens.

vscodePortal.relayUrl.markdownDescription: Relay server for connecting from anywhere, with no Tailscale. Messages are end-to-end encrypted, so the relay can't read them. Leave empty to turn it off.

vscodePortal.wifi.markdownDescription: Also let phones on the **same Wi-Fi** connect directly. Traffic on your local network isn't encrypted, so only turn this on with Wi-Fi you trust.

vscodePortal.screen.markdownDescription: Let paired phones see this Mac's screen and control its mouse and keyboard (the **Screen** tab). macOS asks you to allow **Screen Recording** and **Accessibility** for Visual Studio Code. Run **VSCode Portal: Turn On Screen Sharing** to set it up.

vscodePortal.port.description: Port for the phone server. Other windows use the next free port.

vscodePortal.host.description: Address to listen on. Keep 127.0.0.1 and expose with `tailscale serve`.

vscodePortal.publicUrl.description: The address your phone uses, e.g. https://your-mac.tailnet.ts.net:8443

vscodePortal.token.description: Access code. Leave empty to use a generated one.

vscodePortal.useApiKey.description: Bill Claude prompts to the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your environment. Off by default, so prompts use your Claude subscription (Pro/Max) login instead.

vscodePortal.claudePath.description: Path to the claude CLI. Empty = the one bundled with the Claude Code extension.
